hints: First rewrite the expression as a single linear combination of $\cos x$ and $\sin x$.
Expand $2\cos(x-60^\circ)$ using $\cos(A-B)=\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B$.
Compare the resulting coefficients with $R\cos(x-\alpha)=R\cos x\cos\alpha+R\sin x\sin\alpha$.
Use $R^2=(R\cos\alpha)^2+(R\sin\alpha)^2$ for the exact $R$, then find $\alpha$ from the ratio of the sine and cosine coefficients.
walkthrough:
Expand $\cos(x - 60^\circ)$ using the compound angle identity $\cos(A - B) = \cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B$:
$$\cos(x - 60^\circ) = \cos x\cos 60^\circ + \sin x\sin 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}\cos x + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x$$

Multiply by 2 and add $3\cos x$:
$$3\cos x + 2\cos(x - 60^\circ) = 3\cos x + 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\cos x + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x\right)$$
$$= 3\cos x + \cos x + \sqrt{3}\sin x = 4\cos x + \sqrt{3}\sin x$$

Equate this expression to $R\cos(x - \alpha) = R\cos x\cos\alpha + R\sin x\sin\alpha$:
$$R\cos\alpha = 4$$
$$R\sin\alpha = \sqrt{3}$$

Calculate the exact value of $R$ by summing squares:
$$R^2 = 4^2 + (\sqrt{3})^2 = 16 + 3 = 19$$
$$R = \sqrt{19}$$

Calculate $\alpha$ by dividing the two equations:
$$\tan\alpha = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$$
$$\alpha = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right) \approx \tan^{-1}(0.4330127) \approx 23.4132^\circ \approx 23.41^\circ$$

hints: Use the R-form from part (a) with $x=2\theta$.
Reduce the equation to $\cos(2\theta-\alpha)=\dfrac{2.5}{\sqrt{19}}$, using $\alpha$ at sufficient precision.
Because $0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ$, solve for every value of $2\theta-\alpha$ arising while $0^\circ<2\theta<360^\circ$.
Add $\alpha$, divide each admissible value by $2$, and retain only angles in the stated interval.
walkthrough:
Use the result from part (a) with $x = 2\theta$ to rewrite the equation:
$$\sqrt{19}\cos(2\theta - 23.413^\circ) = 2.5$$
$$\cos(2\theta - 23.413^\circ) = \dfrac{2.5}{\sqrt{19}} \approx 0.573539$$

Find the principal value of the inverse cosine in degrees:
$$\cos^{-1}(0.573539) \approx 55.000^\circ$$

Determine the interval for $2\theta$ and the angle $(2\theta - 23.413^\circ)$:
Since $0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$, we have $0^\circ < 2\theta < 360^\circ$.

Solve for the first angle branch:
$$2\theta - 23.413^\circ = 55.000^\circ$$
$$2\theta = 55.000^\circ + 23.413^\circ = 78.413^\circ$$
$$\theta = \dfrac{78.413^\circ}{2} \approx 39.206^\circ \approx 39.2^\circ$$

Solve for the second angle branch using $360^\circ - 55.000^\circ$:
$$2\theta - 23.413^\circ = 360^\circ - 55.000^\circ = 305.000^\circ$$
$$2\theta = 305.000^\circ + 23.413^\circ = 328.413^\circ$$
$$\theta = \dfrac{328.413^\circ}{2} \approx 164.207^\circ \approx 164.2^\circ$$

State the two solutions in the given interval:
$$\theta = 39.2^\circ \quad \text{and} \quad \theta = 164.2^\circ$$
